Chloe / Redwood team —

Thanks for the demo last week. Per our internal intake, procurement and legal asked me to send an initial sketch of what we think the acceptance path needs to look like so your team can propose sequencing for MSA/DPA -> order form.

We have three tight constraints on our side:
- Clinical data residency confirmation (need DPA to reference our EU data center if we go multi-region)
- Pilot acceptance window (30-day evaluation with two acceptance checkpoints)
- Procurement calendar: we have a finance freeze Aug 10-20 which will block PO creation

Could you map out how the MAP would sequence key milestones (legal review, security questionnaire completion, DPA sign-off, MSA redlines, order form + PO) so we can see handoffs and when we need signatures?

Attached is our internal MAP (simple spreadsheet). Happy to jump on a short call Monday to align.

Thanks,

Medenta Health

Samir —

Appreciate the clear constraints. I sketched a sequenced MAP and checklist that aligns with your procurement freeze and the 30-day pilot. High level (attached):

1) Week 0 - Kickoff & gating
   - Internal kickoff (teams: product, security, procurement)
   - Share evaluation metrics & success criteria (we'll lock prompts and test cases)

2) Week 1 - Security & compliance evidence
   - Redwood provides SOC 2 summary + audit points and DPA template
   - Medenta completes short security questionnaire (we can pre-fill answers for standard items)

3) Week 2 - MSA redline pass + commercial terms
   - Legal redlines collected; Redwood proposes compromise language on data residency and termination
   - Order form template populated with pilot quantities and billing cadence (no PO required for pilot if executed as eval)

4) Week 3 - Pilot run & acceptance checkpoint 1
   - 15-day interim review against success criteria; fix any regressions

5) Week 4 - Final acceptance & sign-off
   - DPA finalization (if required for production region)
   - MSA signature and order form counter-sign 
   - PO submission recommended before Aug 10 finance freeze (we'll plan to get signatures completed by Aug 6)

Notes and risk tradeoffs:
- If Medenta requires DPA-anchored data residency before pilot, that will add ~3 business days for legal review; we can run pilot on pseudonymized data while DPA completes.
- To avoid delay during your finance freeze, prioritized path: get MSA signature + order form countersigned prior to PO issuance. PO can be processed after the freeze if signatures are in place.

I've attached a short sequenced playbook and a redlined MSA excerpt that addresses the residency clause we discussed. Vanessa (cc'd) will own procurement orchestration; Karthik will lead the legal thread for Redwood.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Tuesday 10am PT to walk the MAP and agree on which acceptance gates must be signatures vs. email confirmations. Are you available?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Account Executive

Samir / Chloe —

Thanks — quick alignment from procurement/ops POV:

- We can commit to the timeline Chloe outlined provided we get your legal redlines by EOD Wed (July 15). That gives our legal team two business days to reconcile core MSA/DPA items before the proposed Tue call.
- For order form sequencing: we typically treat the order form as the commercial anchor. If you want to defer PO until after the finance freeze, we need both parties signed order form + countersigned MSA in the system to create the invoice queue.
- Acceptance gates: recommend two signatures only for final acceptance (end of pilot). Interim checkpoint can be a confirmed email from your product owner to keep gating light.

I'll prepare a short procurement checklist and a DocuSign-ready order form template post-call. Chloe — please pull the version with pilot SKUs so I can populate pricing.

Samir — if procurement can provide a single contact for PO/tax/billing (name + email), we'll add them to the DocuSign envelope so cycle time is minimized.
